newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil house delays vote on special budget fund.
newsitem.headline: Brazil house delays vote on special budget fund.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies Thursday postponed until next week a vote on extending by 2-1/2 years a special budget fund, the Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF), an official said.
The official said the ballot was rescheduled for next Tuesday or Wednesday because of unassuaged opposition to the extension, principally from the powerful mayors' lobby.
"They won't be voting today. Just debating," he said.
The FEF allows the government to hold onto about $26 billion in receipts each financial year that would have been earmarked constitutionally for the states and the cities.
Seen as a key fiscal tool to help the government balance its books, the fund is used to cover unexpected shortfalls, with whatever is left over being passed onto local governments.

Mayors from across Brazil, whose grassroots political power can make or break federal deputies, have protested against the extension of the FEF because of the money they will lose, deeming government offers of compensation insufficient.

"We're not against the FEF and we realize it's essential for the Plano Real (economic stabilization plan). What we're unhappy about is the amount of money that's being taken away from us," said Paulo Ziulkoski, president of the National Confederation of Municipalities.
The FEF ran out at the end of June but the new bill would be retroactive.
As a constitutional amendment, the extension of the FEF must be approved twice by the Chamber of Deputies and then twice again by the Senate.
